title: Best Sleep Apps in 2026: An Honest Comparison
description: Best sleep apps in 2026, honestly compared by use case — Sleep Cycle, RISE, Pillow, Calm, Headspace and Sleep Reset — on tracking, sleep debt, falling-asleep content and resetting a slipped schedule, checked against US App Store listings in November 2026.
markdown:
By Anicca · November 2026

Comparison November 2026 · 11 min read By the Anicca Team

The best sleep app in 2026 depends on what is actually wrong with your nights. If you want tracking without a wearable, Sleep Cycle tracks from your phone's microphone and wakes you in light sleep. If you want to know why you are tired, RISE is the only app on this list built around sleep debt and daytime energy. If you wear an Apple Watch, Pillow tracks automatically and records snoring and sleep talking. If your problem is falling asleep rather than measuring sleep, Calm and Headspace are content libraries — sleep stories, sounds and wind-down meditations — not trackers. And if your schedule itself has slipped and you want a score and a plan to reset it, that is the narrower job our own app, Sleep Reset, is built for. Sleep tracking apps can't diagnose sleep conditions. But they can give you data about the amount and type of sleep you're getting, and the right one can tell you what to change.

We reviewed the top sleep apps available today — what each one does well, where each falls short, and which one is right for your nights.

We're going to be upfront: we make one of the apps on this list. Sleep Reset is our app, and we obviously think it's good — but we also know it's not right for everyone, and on the evidence below it is the least proven app here. This comparison is our honest attempt to help you find the app that fits your actual sleep problem, even if that app isn't ours. That is why our own app is listed last, not first, and why its limits are stated in the same format as everyone else's.

## Best sleep apps in 2026

- **Sleep Cycle:** Best Sleep Tracking App Overall
- **RISE:** Best for Sleep Debt and Energy
- **Pillow: Sleep Tracker:** Best Sleep Tracking App for iOS
- **Calm:** Best for Falling Asleep with Stories and Sounds
- **Headspace:** Best for a Wind-Down and Meditation Routine
- **Sleep Reset:** Best for Resetting a Slipped Schedule

## How we tested the best sleep apps

We looked for the following features when choosing the best sleep apps: whether the app tracks sleep at all or only helps you fall asleep, whether it needs a wearable, whether it explains its data or just displays it, what it gives you for free, and whether it is still being maintained. Ratings, rating counts, versions and update dates below were checked against US App Store listings in November 2026. Here's what we found.

We evaluated each app on five factors: core features, whether it goes beyond displaying data, personalization, pricing, and experience quality. One honesty note on method: unlike a hands-on testing lab, this comparison is built from the apps' current store listings, their stated features, and their update records — so where a claim comes from an app's own listing, we say so.

## The Apps, One by One

### Sleep Cycle

Best for: people who want sleep tracking without buying a wearable

Sleep Cycle earned the top spot as our Best Sleep Tracking App Overall, the same verdict the NCOA roundup reached. It uses sound analysis — your phone's microphone — to track sleep, so you don't need a wearable to use it. Its listing describes an AI sleep coach, a sleep tracker and a Smart Alarm that wakes you during your lightest sleep phase, and says the app is built to identify potential sleep issues, show patterns, and help you build a healthier routine. Checked in November 2026: Sleep Cycle - Tracker & Sounds is rated 4.7 from 32,587 ratings on the US App Store, version 6.26.460, last updated 23 November 2026 — updated the same week as this comparison, so it is actively maintained. Its listing claims more than 40 million downloads; that is the developer's figure, not one we can independently verify.

**Strengths**

- No wearable needed — tracking runs from the phone
- Smart alarm wakes you in light sleep
- AI sleep coach in the app
- Available on iOS and Android
- Updated 23 November 2026

**Limitations**

- Sound-based tracking cannot measure heart rate or body temperature without a wearable
- The strongest features sit behind the paid tier on most trackers of this type — check the current listing before relying on the free version
- A smaller US ratings base than Pillow, Calm or Headspace below

Sleep Cycle is best for people who: don't have a wearable; are new to sleep tracking and want data explained; are interested in tracking snoring or sleep sounds; are seeking a gentle wake-up alarm.

### RISE

Best for: people who want to understand sleep debt and daytime energy, not just last night's stages

RISE takes a different angle from every other tracker here: it measures your sleep debt and your energy levels across the day, not only your sleep stages. Its listing says it is the only sleep tracker that also measures sleep debt and energy, that it draws on sleep science, and that it adds widgets, calendar integration, sleeping sounds, meditation guides, smart alarm clocks, habit reminders and a sleep knowledge library. That makes RISE the coaching pick on this page — the app to choose if a sleep score alone has never changed what you do the next day. Checked in November 2026: RISE: Sleep Tracker is rated 4.7 from 74,994 ratings on the US App Store, version 1.654.0, last updated 23 November 2026. Its listing claims over 10 million users and recommendations by sleep publications and professional sports teams; those are the developer's claims, stated here as claims.

**Strengths**

- Sleep debt and energy are the core product, not an add-on
- Habit reminders and calendar integration turn data into a schedule
- Sounds, meditation guides and smart alarm included
- No wearable required
- Updated 23 November 2026

**Limitations**

- Energy predictions are estimates from your history, not measurements of your body
- Less focused on snore and audio-event recording than Pillow
- The coaching model only helps if you act on the schedule it gives you

RISE is best for people who: feel tired without knowing why; want a number for sleep debt, not just sleep stages; want reminders tied to their energy peaks and dips.

### Pillow

Best for: Apple Watch and iPhone users who want automatic tracking and audio events

If you already have an Apple Watch or want to track sleep on your iPhone, Pillow: Sleep Tracker may be a good option. Its listing says Pillow can analyze your sleep cycles automatically using your Apple Watch, iPhone or iPad, work as a smart alarm clock that wakes you at the lightest possible sleep stage, record important audio events such as snoring, sleep apnea sounds and sleep talking, and compare your sleep quality with Apple Health metrics that affect sleep. Checked in November 2026: Pillow: Sleep Tracker is rated 4.4 from 95,857 ratings on the US App Store, version 6.7.4, last updated 19 November 2026. That 4.4 is the lowest rating on this page despite the second-largest tracker ratings base here — read recent reviews before paying, and note that most of its features are understood to sit behind its premium tier.

**Strengths**

- Automatic tracking with Apple Watch — no manual start
- Records snoring, sleep talking and other audio events
- Smart alarm at the lightest sleep stage
- Compares sleep with Apple Health metrics
- Can be used without a wearable, from iPhone or iPad

**Limitations**

- Available on Apple products only
- Lowest US App Store rating on this page (4.4)
- Free version is limited compared with the paid tier

Pillow is best for people who: already use an Apple Watch; want snoring and sleep-talking recordings; are iOS users who want tracking to start on its own.

### Calm

Best for: people whose problem is falling asleep, not measuring sleep

Calm is not primarily a sleep tracker, and it is more honest to list it as what it is: the largest sleep-content library on this page. Its listing calls it the #1 app for sleep, meditation and relaxation, and its signature feature is Sleep Stories — bedtime stories for adults — alongside sleep sounds, deep sleep music and mindfulness programs for insomnia and stress. If you lie awake with a racing mind, a story that gives your mind something dull to follow can do more than a sleep-stage graph. Checked in November 2026: Calm is rated 4.8 from 1,996,159 ratings on the US App Store, version 7.6, last updated 18 November 2026 — by far the largest ratings base here. Its listing claims 180 million downloads worldwide; that is the developer's figure.

**Strengths**

- Largest ratings base on this page by a wide margin
- Sleep Stories, sounds and music built specifically for falling asleep
- Also covers meditation, stress and anxiety, not only sleep
- Available on iOS and Android

**Limitations**

- Content library, not a dedicated sleep tracker — it will not explain your sleep debt
- The full library requires a subscription
- Easy to keep consuming content without changing the schedule underneath

Calm is best for people who: cannot switch their mind off at night; want stories and sounds rather than data; want one app for sleep and daytime stress.

### Headspace

Best for: people who want an expert-led wind-down and meditation routine

Headspace, like Calm, is a mental-health and meditation app with a serious sleep offer rather than a tracker. Its listing describes expert-led sleep tools alongside more than 500 guided meditations, courses and programs for stress, anxiety and sleep trouble, plus an empathetic AI companion and access to coaches and licensed therapists for further support. Where Calm leads on stories, Headspace leads on structure: courses and guided practice that build a repeatable wind-down. Checked in November 2026: Headspace: Sleep & Meditation is rated 4.8 from 973,724 ratings on the US App Store, version 8.42.1, last updated 23 November 2026 — the joint-highest rating on this page, on nearly a million ratings.

**Strengths**

- Joint-highest US App Store rating here (4.8) on 973,724 ratings
- Structured, expert-led programs rather than only loose content
- Sleep tools inside a wider mental-health practice
- Updated 23 November 2026

**Limitations**

- Meditation-first app — sleep tracking is not its core job
- Full access requires a subscription
- More than a restless sleeper may need, if all you want is a tracker

Headspace is best for people who: want a guided routine, not just sounds; are dealing with stress and anxiety alongside poor sleep; prefer courses with a beginning and an end.

### Sleep Reset

Best for: people whose sleep schedule itself has slipped — travel, shift changes, late nights — and who want a score and a plan to reset it

Sleep Reset is our app, listed last because we publish this page. It does a narrower job than the trackers above, and its own product page says so plainly: you answer onboarding questions about your goals to get a free sleep reset score and a recovery outlook, and a paid subscription unlocks a personalized reset plan, bedtime timing, guided breathwork and next-morning recovery steps. It is a general-wellness app, not medical advice, and it does not treat insomnia. See it at https://aniccaai.com/sleepreset and in our full product list at https://aniccaai.com/dais . Checked in November 2026: For Better Sleep - Sleep Reset is rated 0 from 0 ratings on the US App Store, version 1.0.4, last updated 12 November 2026, listed for iPhone and requiring iOS 18.0 or later. Zero ratings means exactly what it says: there is no user track record to point to yet, and you should weigh that against every other app on this page.

**Strengths**

- Free sleep reset score and recovery outlook, no subscription needed for the score
- Built for one specific problem — a disrupted schedule — rather than general tracking
- Personalized plan, bedtime timing and guided breathwork in one flow
- No wearable required

**Limitations**

- No US App Store ratings yet — the smallest track record on this page, at zero
- The personalized plan, bedtime timing, guided breathwork and recovery steps require a paid subscription
- iPhone only, and requires iOS 18.0 or later
- Not a sleep tracker and not a treatment for insomnia

Sleep Reset is best for people who: are recovering from travel, shift work or a run of late nights; want a single score and a plan instead of a dashboard; want to start free and decide after seeing the score.

## How to Choose the Right App

The best sleep app is the one that matches your actual problem. A few questions that help narrow it down, in the order the winning roundups ask them:

**What is your budget?** Most sleep apps offer a free version with basic features and a paid subscription with much more data. If you're not sure whether the paid subscription is worth it, a free trial or a genuinely free first step can help you decide. On this page, Sleep Reset's score and recovery outlook are free, Sleep Cycle, RISE and Pillow are free to download with paid tiers, and Calm and Headspace are free to download with their full libraries behind a subscription. We have not listed subscription prices here because they change and differ by plan — check the current price on the store listing before you commit.

**Is the data representation clear?** More sleep data isn't always more useful. Some apps show so much information that it's hard to tell what matters. RISE reduces the night to sleep debt and energy, which many people find easier to act on; Pillow and Sleep Cycle show fuller stage data, which rewards a closer read.

**Do you want additional features, or one job done well?** Sleep coaching, smart alarms, snore tracking, heart rate and sleep-stage tracking and sleep scores are the shared feature set of the trackers. Content apps add stories, sounds and meditation instead. A reset app does one job — getting a slipped schedule back — and stops there.

**Do you want a smart alarm?** A smart alarm is designed to wake you during a lighter period of sleep within a time window you choose, so you start the day less groggy. Sleep Cycle, RISE and Pillow all offer one; the content and reset apps on this page are not built around alarms.

**Is it compatible with your devices?** Sleep Cycle, RISE, Calm and Headspace are available on iOS and Android. Pillow is Apple only. Sleep Reset is iPhone only and requires iOS 18.0 or later. Check whether your specific wearable is compatible before relying on any app for heart-rate data.

## Our Take

We built Sleep Reset because we noticed that every sleep app was doing one of two things: measuring your sleep in ever more detail, or playing you content until you drifted off. Neither one answers the question people actually ask after a trip, a shift change or a bad week — "my schedule is broken, what do I do tonight, and tomorrow morning?" A free score, a recovery outlook, and then a plan with bedtime timing, breathwork and next-morning steps is our attempt at that third job.

We're obviously biased. But the honest version of this page is the table at the top: if you want tracking, take Sleep Cycle or Pillow; if you want to understand your tiredness, take RISE; if you want help falling asleep, take Calm or Headspace. Sleep Reset only earns its place if your schedule itself is the problem — and with zero US ratings so far, it has the most to prove of any app here.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is the best sleep app in 2026?**

A: There is no single best sleep app — it depends on your problem. For tracking without a wearable, Sleep Cycle is the strongest all-round pick. For understanding sleep debt and daytime energy, RISE is the specialist. For Apple Watch owners, Pillow tracks automatically. For falling asleep, Calm and Headspace are content libraries rather than trackers. For resetting a schedule that has slipped, Sleep Reset is the narrow specialist — and the least proven option here.

**Q: Do you always need a subscription for sleep tracking apps?**

A: No. The apps on this page are all free to download, and some give you useful information without paying — Sleep Reset's score and recovery outlook are free, for example. A paid subscription usually unlocks historical trends, fuller tracking, content libraries or personalized plans, and what sits behind the paywall varies by app, so check the current listing.

**Q: How accurate are sleep apps?**

A: Sleep apps estimate sleep from sound, movement and — with a wearable — heart rate. They can show patterns consistent with how you feel, and pairing a tracker with a wearable often improves the picture, especially for heart rate and interruptions. But sleep tracking apps are not substitutes for polysomnography, a clinical sleep study used to evaluate sleep disorders. If you suspect a condition like sleep apnea, talk to your doctor.

**Q: Is sleep tracking bad for anxiety?**

A: For some people, having sleep data is soothing. For others, focusing too much on sleep scores can increase sleep-related anxiety — sometimes called orthosomnia, the anxious chasing of a perfect score. If a dashboard makes you more anxious, a content app like Calm or Headspace, or a one-off reset plan like Sleep Reset, may suit you better than nightly tracking. If you're concerned, talk to your doctor or therapist before getting a sleep tracking app.
